gap: No result ChatGPT got states that a LiFePO4 station claiming a ≤10 ms UPS switchover with 980 W pass-through (BLUETTI Elite 30 V2) costs $289.99 on the maker's store, the same money as the 1500 VA lead-acid UPSes it recommended, or that EcoFlow's own store sells the DELTA 3 Classic (same 1,024 Wh, 1,800 W and 10 ms auto-switch claim) at $479, $100 below the $579 DELTA 3 it showed.
standout_why: I compared against the cited Bambu forum thread 'Power Interruption Alert! Which UPS for a P1S+AMS?' (forum.bambulab.com/t/41205), which names models (CP1500PFCLCD, a 750 VA unit, APC Smart-UPS 1500, a 2000 VA/1200 W unit) but gives no prices and no measured transfer times, and against the Bambu spec and quick-start PDFs, which have no backup-device content. Only ChatGPT's own cards had prices (CyberPower $239.95, APC $299.99/$339.99, DELTA 3 $579, Anker C1000 $449.99, and an unpriced AC180). None of them puts a maker-store price on a ≤10 ms LiFePO4 unit at UPS money, or mentions the cheaper DELTA 3 Classic.
decides: This reframes the flicker pick. At the same price as a CyberPower or APC 1500 VA UPS, the Elite 30 V2 claims the same class of switchover (≤10 ms). Its 980 W pass-through covers the P1S's 350 W maximum at 110 V, and it holds about 245 usable Wh (about 1.6 h at 150 W) where the lead-acid UPSes give tens of minutes. For whole-print outages, the 1 kWh pick at the maker's price becomes the DELTA 3 Classic at $479 (10 ms claim) instead of the $579 DELTA 3. The AC180 ($499) and P1800 ($399) are cheaper per Wh, but our page records a 20 ms switchover for both, double the 10 ms claims.

findings.source_title: BLUETTI Elite 30 V2 Portable Power Station | 600W 288Wh (Blush Pink)
findings.note: Maker's claim: 'Seamless switch with 980W bypass power'. The 980 W bypass is above the P1S's 350 W maximum at 110 V (Bambu spec, also holmes4's ~350 W startup peak on 120 V in forum thread 41205). Runtime: 288 Wh × 0.85 ÷ 150 W ≈ 1.6 h. Where it loses: 288 Wh won't finish a long print.
